title: WASD Crowd
cue: crowds in one draw call; birds, fish, butterflies
summary: Crowds of one animated model, its clips baked once into textures, so hundreds of copies play them with no skeleton, each in its own clip, pace, and tint; and flocks of birds, fish, and butterflies.
useWhen: Many copies of one animated character are on screen at once: an army, a horde, spectators, townsfolk, a herd. Or a world needs life in the background: birds overhead, fish under water, butterflies over a meadow. A hundred skinned characters stall a Web build; a thousand crowd members do not.
avoidWhen: A handful of characters, or ones the player fights or talks to up close, which need skeletons for ragdolls, attachments, and blending: use wasd-character there.
